annotators.primary: devin-visual-v2-wave-a (cases.json verification.by for TA; annotator field in L-verdicts-*.json for ownership — same annotator on both tasks, so this overlap measures one annotator pair, not a pool)

protocolStatement: Second-annotator verdicts were frozen to ta-overlap.json / ownership-overlap.json BEFORE any primary verdict value or note was read. Selection touched only caseId/split/situation/verification.by (TA) and caseId/tMs/owners-index-keys (ownership). K-summary.json / L-summary.json contents and the ownership-review.json sidecar were not opened pre-freeze.

ta.mapping: primary verification.state → taxonomy: verified→correct-lock, rejected→reject (no primary note among the 12 indicated wrong-person, so no primary wrong-lock present)

kappa3Class.honestCaveats: n=12 with 11/12 primary correct-lock: pe=0.70 is prevalence-dominated, kappa is unstable (95% CI roughly ±0.71 — statistically uninformative). Raw agreement + qualitative disagreement analysis carry the signal at this n.

disagreements.w14: wrong-lock (lime on phone-filming staffer; live ARMY player is the plausible region occupant)
disagreements.primary: verified (note: 'black-shirt staff filming on phone behind barrier IS target … occlusion-heavy bystander case')
disagreements.perceptionAgreement: FULL — both annotators independently identified the same person (phone-filming staffer) under the lime box
disagreements.divergence: definitional: is TA gold 'region→person correspondence (any human)' or 'region→valid gameplay target'?
disagreements.adjudicationLean: PRIMARY, conditional: under the bench's operational question ('did we lock the person the user aimed the region at?') a bystander-occupant is a legitimate adversarial case. But this definition is currently unwritten, and such cases need a situation tag (e.g. bystander_target) so lock-correct metrics can be sliced; silently counting them as ordinary correct-locks would flatter product metrics.

disagreements.adjudicationLean: PRIMARY, same condition: keep as adversarial case ONLY with an explicit bystander_target tag + written definition; otherwise reject.

ownership.mapping: primary 4-class → W14 3-class: target→TARGET, other→NOT_TARGET, reject→NOT_TARGET, ambiguous→AMBIGUOUS. W14 sub-tags (other_player_paddle vs not_a_paddle) allow a 4-class reconstruction.

kappa3Class.honestCaveats: 31 boxes but clustered within 12 frames of 3 videos — effective n is lower than 31 and the nominal SE understates uncertainty. Marginals happen to be symmetric (7/22/2 both sides).

kappa4Class.note: 4-class kappa exceeds 3-class because chance agreement drops when NOT_TARGET splits into other/reject

disagreements.w14: AMBIGUOUS — box mostly on background right of target's motion-blur core; a center-point label would miss the paddle
disagreements.primary: target — 'box clips the blur's right edge, center ~.03 norm right of blur center (acceptable)'
disagreements.perceptionAgreement: same object hypothesis (target's motion-blurred rising paddle); divergence is the center-offset acceptance THRESHOLD
disagreements.adjudicationLean: PRIMARY plausibly right (offset within the bench's center-error tolerance), but the numeric acceptance rule (e.g. 'accept if box center within 0.03-0.05 norm of visible paddle mass') exists only in the primary's head — must go into guidelines or motion-blur frames will drift by annotator.

disagreements.w14: NOT_TARGET(other_player_paddle, conf 0.6) — white paddle-like blur above far barrier
disagreements.primary: ambiguous — 'likely a far-court player's paddle mid-swing but no resolvable hand'
disagreements.perceptionAgreement: same object hypothesis; divergence is the evidence standard for committing to 'other' vs downgrading to 'ambiguous'
disagreements.adjudicationLean: PRIMARY — schema intent is that uncommittable boxes stay out of P/R; guideline should require resolvable hand/arm continuity before 'other'.

disagreements.w14: TARGET (conf 0.75) — dark paddle flat at hip height in front of target's hanging hand
disagreements.primary: reject — 'dark GROUND paddle lying flat at target's feet, NO owner (static since 1303 — 3rd occurrence)'
disagreements.perceptionAgreement: GENUINE perception disagreement — the only one in the ownership set
disagreements.adjudicationLean: PRIMARY almost certainly right: temporal evidence (object static across ≥2s, seen in 3 frames) is decisive and was unavailable under W14's single-frame protocol. A floor paddle beside a hand is visually near-identical to a held paddle in one frame. This is the documented failure mode of single-frame ownership review.

guidelineRecommendations: TA: write the operational definition — verified = 'lime track is the person occupying the start region', regardless of player status; ADD a required situation tag bystander_target for non-player occupants so product metrics can slice them. (Resolves both TA disagreements.)

TA: for crowd-heavy regions where the target only clips the region edge at mid-frame (faead-s3w5-p2 pattern), require a 3-frame scrub (start/mid/end renders) before verifying — single mid-frame is insufficient.
TA: define precedence when both apply: wrong-person beats unusable-scene beats correct (annotators need a deterministic order).

Ownership: single-frame review is NOT safe for ownership — require ±1-2 adjacent frames (or the propose tool emitting a 3-frame strip) plus a static-object ledger; floor paddles, net-tape patches and banner graphics are named repeat traps (all three appeared in this 12-frame sample).
Ownership: write the numeric center-offset acceptance rule for motion-blurred paddles (primary used ~0.03 norm; codify a threshold).
Ownership: 'other' requires resolvable hand/arm continuity; otherwise 'ambiguous'. Union boxes spanning two paddles are always 'reject' (geometry, not ownership).
Both: record annotator confidence per verdict (W14 did; primary schema has no field) — low-confidence agreements (0.5-0.6) are where the next disagreements hide.
